It's is better for those that are good at something to be separated from those that are bad, and this can be proven mathematically.

Suppose you have four people performing a task. Two of the people will complete the task perfectly 100% of the time, while the other two people will complete the task perfectly only 50% of the time. Which is better: one team with both of the 100% workers and one team with both of the 50% workers, or two teams with a 100% worker and a 50% worker?

In the first case team one will complete the task 100% (100% x 100%) of the time, as both will execute the task perfectly. Team two on the other hand, will only complete the task 25% of the time (50% x 50%) because half of the time one person fails and the other half of the time the other person fails. The combined success rate of the two teams in this case is 125%.

In the second case, both teams will be successful 50% of the time, because one person will always complete the task and the other person will only complete the task 50% of the time causing the first person to fail. The combined success rate in this case is 100% (50% + 50%).

As we have just demonstrated, diversity is mathematically worse.
